note: Seeded 2026-09-22. Curl-only environment: Bing RSS degrades after roughly one query per session and DuckDuckGo serves a challenge, so the SERP was run once and then every source was fetched and read directly. Reddit is blocked, so tier E is empty and is recorded as such rather than quietly omitted. Scope ruling, edge cases and open venue questions live in data/topics/west-african.json.
scope: West Africa only: Nigeria, Ghana, Senegal, The Gambia, Sierra Leone, Ivory Coast and their neighbours, plus diaspora kitchens rooted in the region. Ethiopian, Eritrean, Somali and Kenyan (East), Moroccan, Algerian, Tunisian and Libyan (North), Congolese (Central) and South African and Mauritian (Southern) names were dropped at extraction from the African-wide lists. Venues outside Greater London were dropped by name.

sources.name: Michelin Guide 2026 - Greater London, African selection
sources.readVia: READ FROM THE AWARDING BODY DIRECTLY, 2026-09-22. guide.michelin.com is listed under blocked.permanent403 in data/sources.json and that entry is WRONG: it answers plain `curl -sL` with HTTP 200 and full HTML. What produces the HTTP 202 empty body is sending a Chrome user agent. Fetch with NO -A flag. The Wikipedia substitute was not needed and is stars-only, which is why the Bib Gourmand had gone missing from every previous pass.

quotes.Chishuru: One Star: High quality cooking, 2026 MICHELIN Guide United Kingdom. Cuisine: African. Price: ££££. Inspector: 'Adejoke Bakare's West African restaurant continues to go from strength to strength in this warm, bright Fitzrovia spot which comes with a real neighbourhood feel.' 3 Great Titchfield Street, W1W 8AX.
quotes.Akoko: One Star: High quality cooking, 2026 MICHELIN Guide United Kingdom. Cuisine: African. Inspector quotes the founder: 'We aim to prove that West African cuisine deserves its place in fine dining by highlighting its unique flavours and culinary traditions on its own terms,' says founder Aji Akokomi. 21 Berners Street, W1T 3LP.
quotes.Akara: Bib Gourmand: good quality, good value cooking, 2026 MICHELIN Guide United Kingdom. Cuisine: African, Brazilian. Price: ££. Good for: solo dining. Inspector: 'The team from Akoko are behind this appealing restaurant tucked underneath the arches in Borough Yards. An akara is a black-eyed pea fritter commonly found in West African and Brazilian cuisine.' Arch 208, 18 Stoney Street, Borough Market, SE1 9AD. THIS RESOLVES THE OPEN QUESTION: London x London's Bib claim is correct and London Best Eats' 'Good Cooking' label is not.

sources.theFinding: MICHELIN'S GREATER LONDON AFRICAN SELECTION IS EXACTLY THREE RESTAURANTS AND ALL THREE HOLD A DISTINCTION. The filter page prints '3 restaurants'. Two one-stars and one Bib Gourmand, and two of the three have the same owner, Aji Akokomi. Trap 15 checked: the page also links MRBL, Bar des Pres Mayfair and AO by Daniel Rogan in Southampton - those are the 'you might also like' rail, not the list, and the Southampton one gives it away.
sources.ikoyiIsNotInIt: IKOYI IS NOT IN MICHELIN'S AFRICAN SELECTION AND THAT IS THE CLEANEST EVIDENCE IN THE TOPIC. Its own Michelin page reads 'Two Stars: Excellent cooking restaurant in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide United Kingdom' with Cuisine: CREATIVE. Not African. Wikipedia's starred list labels it West African, the awarding body does not. Ikoyi's two stars are still a real dated fact and are printed as such; Michelin is NOT counted as a West African citation for it.

declined.reason: TRAP 2 - SYNDICATION. The body is Time Out's article reproduced verbatim, 'Time Out tip' lines and all, posted under 'Submitted by daniel'. Time Out is the source and is already counted. Counting this would give one masthead two votes.

A FILTERABLE DIRECTORY, NOT AN OPINION - and it is registered tier C in data/sources.json, so this needs a human decision. The page is generated by a cuisine filter, each venue carries an aggregated star score (4.8, 4.6, 4.5) and a price band, and the copy is a one-line 'At its core:' summary. Same call as blackeatsldn.com on Caribbean and dinehalal.uk on halal. It is still useful as a LEAD: it is where Spinach & Agushi in Exmouth Market surfaced, and no countable source in this pass names that venue.

SEO CONTENT FARM. Title assembled from keywords ('28 Best African Restaurants in London (Nigerian, Ethiopian, Ghanaian, Moroccan & More)'), US spellings throughout on a London site ('cozy', 'colorful', 'flavorful'), no evidence of a visit anywhere in 28 entries, 'ALSO SEE:' keyword links mid-list, and a byline of 'Bianca' with no bio. Fails the data/serp/README test on three counts. Not in data/sources.json; should go in `excluded`.

COMPILATION CHANNEL, AND IT IS REGISTERED TIER D IN data/sources.json, so this also needs a human decision. Its 'Top 10 Best African Restaurants in London' carries the disclaimer 'We have used video footage and images to maximize the clarity of the content ... Footage, music, image, and graphics used in the video belong to their respective owners.' No visit, no named creator, stock music. The video tier's equivalent of an SEO farm.
Single-venue review ('I visited London's only Senegalese restaurant'), not a round-up. Same call as the Caribbean pass made on single-venue features.
Aggregator, excluded globally. Ranked second on the head-term SERP.
Directory listing pages ('Top 20 Senegalese Restaurants In London'). No byline, no visits.
